To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The heterogeneous reactions of deltamethrine and permethrin with ozone in the atmosphere result in different products.
the heterogeneous ozonolyses of deltamethin and permethrin are mainly influenced by presence of the cyono moiety at the alpha-position of deltamthrin (pyretrhod type II) and the role of water.
the heterogeneous reaction of gas-phase ozone with deltamethrin produces phosgene, bromophosgene and 3-PBA, while permethrin produces phospene.

the heterogeneous reactions of two commonly used pyrethrods with gas-phase ozone in the atmosphere.
the heterogeneous reactions of pesticides in the atmosphere.
the heterogeneous ozonolyses of two pyrethroids, deltamethrine and permethrin and the identification of their degradation products.

the ozonolyses of deltamethin and permethrin in aqueous aerosol droplets are complex and involve multiple reactions and products.
the ozonolyses of deltamethin and permethrin lead to the formation of a wide range of products with different chemical properties, including some highly toxic and hazardous compounds.
deltamethrin is more sensitive to heterogeneous ozonolyses than permethrin and its degradation products are more toxic than permethrin.

the ozonolyses of deltamethin and permethrin in the atmosphere can produce toxic intermediates and products, and the presence of water can accelerate the degradation of pyrethroids and increase the toxicity of the intermediates and products.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of water is essential for the heterogeneous reactions between ozone and pyrethroids.
the presence of the α-cyano moiety in pyrethroid molecules can lead to different mechanisms and products in the heterogeneous reactions of these pesticides with ozone.

the heterogeneous ozonolysed pyrethroids can pose further health and/or environmental hazard due to the emergence of their degradation products, some of them are more toxic than the parent compounds, which can lead to a significant increase of the toxicity of the particle phase.
